notes: Company snapshot: mid-market CX SaaS, multi-tenant helpdesk + chat (proprietary UI). ~50k user-facing chats/day peak, heavy spikes during product incidents.
Primary goal: automated chat deflection + lightweight agent assist to reduce live-agent load by 50-60% while keeping SLA for reply <2s for agent assist flows.
Workloads: high-volume short-turn chat deflection (templated + contextual), ticket summarization for downstream triage, tool-calling for backend ops (issue create, KB search).
Performance targets: 95th pct latency target <=700ms for deflection decisions; agent-assist target <=200ms interactive for live agents during handoff.
Cost sensitivity: unit economics analysis required. CFO expects POC demonstrating <=$0.0008 per deflected message on steady-state 24/7 traffic. Interested in quantization + batching to hit numbers.
Model preferences: prefers open LLMs with proven 4-bit/8-bit quantized variants; fallback routing to smaller Llama-style models on spikes. Wants Redwood to show quantized throughput profiles.
Routing/fallback needs: region-aware routing (US primary, EU for EU customers), automatic fallback to smaller model family under capacity pressure, circuit-breaker when latency >1.5s.
Reliability & spikes: Zero-tolerance for long tail outages — require auto-scaling + graceful degradation (e.g., cached templated replies) during incident spikes. Stress tests needed.

Caching & batching requirements: aggressive prefix/KV caching for repeated flows (account lookups, order status), recommended batching for background reranking/embeddings jobs to reduce per-unit cost.

Security/compliance: SSO/SAML, customer-level audit logs, KMS integration for key management, data residency = US primary, 90-day ephemeral retention for PII fields; legal asked for data processing addendum.
POC scope: 6 weeks. Week 1 integration (webhook + tooling), Weeks 2-3 baseline metrics + latency/cost profiling, Weeks 4-5 spike/load testing and fallback validation, Week 6 ROI report + playbook.
